summary: An announcement that the SURVEY program at MIT-DMCG, which regularly checks whether ARPANET server hosts are working, was running again. It now checks every 20 minutes instead of 15 and fully completes the initial connection protocol. Sites can ask to be left out or added. It was updated by RFC 530.

eli5.summary: A program that regularly knocks on every computer's door to see who is home is back, now knocking a little less often.

questions: what is the arpanet survey program
how often did survey check hosts
subtitle: The SURVEY host-checking program at MIT-DMCG is running again, now every 20 minutes.

tldr.problem: Network users needed to know which server hosts were up, and the SURVEY program had been down and then caused trouble with incomplete connections.
tldr.mechanism: SURVEY at MIT-DMCG polls listed hosts every 20 minutes, completes the initial connection protocol, and publishes results through a NETSTATUS service on socket 15.
tldr.outcome: Sites can ask to be added or left out, and RFC 530 later updated this announcement.

today: RFC 523 is an announcement with no formal status recorded, and it was updated by RFC 530.

sections.title: SURVEY Is Back
sections.content:
Abhay Bhushan announces that the survey program at the MIT-DMCG computer system is in operation. Hosts are now surveyed every 20 minutes instead of the earlier 15 minutes.

Some sites had problems with incomplete ICPs when survey first came up. The author says the problem has been fixed, and asks to be told if any site is being inconvenienced. On written request he will not survey a particular server site, and on oral or written request he will add sites that want to be surveyed.
sections.eli5: The checking program is running again. If it bothers you, ask the owner to stop knocking on your door.

sections.title: How the Survey Works
sections.content:
Survey issues an RFC to socket 1 and now goes through the complete ICP, which establishes Telnet connections and then closes them. The response time is therefore the time to establish the Telnet connections, so larger numbers than before are expected and, the author thinks, more accurate.

The sites then surveyed were hosts 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 23, 31, 32, 35, 65, 66, 69, 70, 74, 78, 86, 133, 134, 138 and 198, numbered in decimal.
sections.eli5: The program does not just ring the doorbell, it walks all the way in and says hello, so it takes a little longer.

sections.title: The NETSTATUS Service
sections.content:
A NETSTATUS service is provided on socket 15 (decimal) of host 70. An ICP to it returns a header line with month, day, year, hour and minute, then lines of host number, code and response time in tenths of a second. The list ends with -1, and the connection is closed right after the data is sent.

The output is designed for both people and programs. Users can also log in to DMCG and use the NETWRK subsystem to display the data in many formats (see RFC 308). The data is also recorded on the DATACOMPUTER (CCA).
sections.eli5: You can also ask the program for a list, one line per computer, saying how fast each one answered.
